attack_summary: Each re-examination condition is tested against the lane's own §4v-derived standard: a condition nobody is tasked to watch, at a named venue, on a cadence, is prose with correct grammar. Classifications (conceded in Q60) are not re-litigated; only the conditions' checkability is attacked.
audit_role: non-author audit of a ruling that reverses my Q55 finding

amendment.cadence: every future non-author audit of RULING.md (standing practice; R5 precedent verified such audits happen and bite)
amendment.condition_as_written: Restore as an enforceable gate when a conductor proposes to kill another pane's candidate. The kill receipt must identify the non-author concurrence before the ruling lands.
amendment.defect: Self-policing: the watcher (the proposing conductor) is the constrained party. No venue, no cadence, no independent checker. A kill receipt that omits the concurrence fails silently — nothing rejects it.
amendment.required_fix: Attach to the RULED_OUT recording venue: any RULED_OUT entry whose killer differs from the candidate author must cite the concurrence in the entry; the next ruling-audit verifies presence. Until attached, this condition is prose.
amendment.watcher: none named (self-policing by the proposing conductor)

amendment.cadence: any §5 score edit; verified at next score-table review
amendment.condition_as_written: Re-promote only when a receipt or dispatch conflates a resolved prerequisite with a changed score; attach the exact conflicting fields and require a separate score receipt.
amendment.defect: Conflations are what readers miss (cf. §3w family: per-case conclusions from aggregates). Nobody is tasked to scan receipts/dispatches for score-on-resolution events. If the condition cannot fire observably, DEMOTE-with-unwatched-return is DELETE with extra steps — the ruling's decision-rule uses these conditions as load-bearing (what makes demote≠delete), so they inherit gate-grade burden.
amendment.required_fix: Attach to the score-change venue: any §5/STATUS score edit whose basis is a hold-resolution event must cite the separate score receipt in the edit; next auditor checks score-edit lineage. Weakest of the three even after amendment — stated as such, not smoothed.

amendment.cadence: at the promotion attempt itself (self-announcing event)
amendment.condition_as_written: At the first promotion attempt, run all four rung-5 conditions with a non-conductor owner and a project-level kill criterion. After that attempt, audit whether the gate is satisfiable and outcome-changing.
amendment.defect: Only in the follow-up: 'audit whether satisfiable' names no auditor. The trigger itself is fine — a promotion attempt (deep plan emission for a rungs-1–4-cleared candidate) is loud and visible in STATUS.tsv/PLAN; anyone reading the lane sees it.
amendment.required_fix: Promotion packet must include the four-condition run + named owner + project kill criterion, else the promotion is out-of-order by rule; name the promotion reviewer as the satisfiability auditor in that packet. Smallest fix of the three.
amendment.watcher: the promotion reviewer (unnamed until the packet exists — acceptable: the event creates its watcher)

interest_disclosure: INTERESTED PARTY: I authored GAUNTLET_SPEC_MU.md whose deletion candidates this ruling demotes-or-keeps instead of deleting. This audit attacks the ruling's re-examination conditions, not its classifications (conceded in CONCEDE_spec_audit_MU.md). A reversal-against-interest concession plus a genuine attack is worth more than either alone; a retaliatory audit is worth nothing, and the per-condition verdicts below are the evidence this is the former.
limits: Did not re-verify the §3h-precedent reasoning beyond the dead-vs-dormant distinction (conceded in Q60).
Watcher proposals are amendments demanded, not mechanisms verified — cadence/venue adoption is a future unit's work.
steelman: Demotion-to-guidance correctly lowers the enforcement claim, so demanding gate-grade checkability of mere guidance may be category error: guidance plus a concrete return predicate beats a deleted rule. Held against: the ruling's own decision-rule makes these conditions load-bearing (they are what distinguishes demote from delete), so they inherit the burden. If they are mere guidance, all three rules are one quiet session from de facto deletion.
